asus-rog-flow-z13-gz302ea.title: ASUS ROG Flow Z13 (2025) GZ302EA (AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S)
asus-rog-flow-z13-gz302ea.image_name_comment: golden/windows/build.sh names this laptop's golden image zero-<tier>-windows-<image_name>.img.zst when it is not the tier's default laptop (the HP ZBook Ultra G1a is), so both can sit in the bucket.
asus-rog-flow-z13-gz302ea.hardware_comment: UNTESTED ON HARDWARE. Same silicon as the HP ZBook Ultra G1a (Strix Halo, Radeon 8060S = PCI\VEN_1002&DEV_1586; ASUS subsystems 15141043/17141043/17241043/1FB31043 are listed by both the ASUS and the AMD display INF). Wi-Fi/Bluetooth MediaTek MT7925 (PCI\VEN_14C3&DEV_7925), audio Realtek ALC3251 + Cirrus CS35L51 amplifiers + Dolby Atmos APO, touchpad/keyboard folio ASUS Precision TouchPad + ASUS HID filters, hotkeys/power modes ASUS System Control Interface v3 (ACPI\ASUS2018/ASUS2025) + Armoury Crate Control Interface (ACPI\ASUS9001). No OEM driver pack exists: ASUS publishes one package per device from rog.asus.com/support/webapi/ProductV2/GetPDDrivers (model ROG-Flow-Z13-2025, m1id 30858, osid 52 = Windows 11 64-bit), which also publishes each package's sha256; every sha256 below was re-computed from the download. Every ASUS package is a signed wrapper .exe (NSIS, or an Inno Setup stub that runs pnputil) around ONE embedded 7-Zip archive holding plain INF driver folders: extract 'asus-7z' carves and unpacks that archive without running anything. Left out on purpose (applications, not drivers; the Store or Armoury Crate installs them): MyASUS, Armoury Crate & Aura Creator installer, Virtual Assistant, Aura Wallpaper, ASUS Smart Display Control, ScreenXpert, GlideX, Realtek Codec Console (Store). The MediaTek Bluetooth package (Bluetooth_ROG_MediaTek_Z_V1.1045.0.566Sub1_47887.exe, sha256 6bbfed09217f1f12a419854931474d6e5fc496458e9e97eff71e7f9a21e92316, 26,530,224 bytes) unpacks to the same WLAN+BT+ACX folders as the WLAN package, so it is not injected twice.
